published_prior_art.cite: GabrielSachsSjolander2025 gives two- and three-level-IV target-contrast invariance; SongGuoChanRichardson2024 treats arbitrary categorical exposures under full exclusion.
BalkePearl1997: sharp binary-IV response-type bounds for the ATE.
GabrielSachsSjolander2025 motivates the distinction between target and contaminated/off-target levels, but does not give this saturated-versus-common-response LP certificate.
SongGuoChanRichardson2024 studies the full categorical multinomial model; Blackwell1953 is generic experiment-comparison theory, not this target-only nuisance factorization.
Blackwell1953 supplies generic kernel comparisons, but not equality after a parameter-dependent allocation nuisance is maximized out.
SongGuoChanRichardson2024 provides categorical-IV KL-projection inference under full exclusion; the claimed advance is its target-only quotient application.
Hoffman1952 and Li1993 give generic polyhedral error-bound and RHS-sensitivity tools; the causal reduced-fiber specialization is additional but derivative.
LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 and Gafarov2025 treat nonsmooth IV/affine-bound inference, but not the claimed target-only quotient lower experiment.
Gafarov2025 gives regularized uniformly valid inference for affine polygonal identified sets; the unresolved delta is an exact target-IV local minimax phase diagram and adaptive attainment.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 1 (thm:quotient-sharpness)
novelty_flags.one_line: The advertised strict extension is against GabrielSachsSjolander2025 alone; SongGuoChanRichardson2024 is only described as informed-by, so the flagship framing lacks a second strict comparator or a generic-class promotion.

soundness_flags.label: def:full-model; thm:quotient-sharpness
soundness_flags.one_line: The model does not require P(Z=z)>0 for every z, yet p_z=P(X=x,Y=y|Z=z), s_z, and the universal identification claim require those conditional arm laws to be defined.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Result 1 concerns a two-level IV with two target levels and one ill-defining or contaminated level; Result 3 concerns a three-level IV with two well-defining target levels and one such off-target level. The paper does not state an arbitrary-cardinality complete-law quotient.

The paper considers categorical X, Y, and Z, characterizes the joint law of potential outcomes for all treatment categories, and supplies KL-tail-based confidence regions for convex functions of that law.
The paper gives a regularized support-function estimator with uniform Gaussian limits and uniformly valid confidence sets for affine polygonal identified sets, including nonregular cases.

The paper studies binary-IV Balke--Pearl bounds with covariates, derives margin-condition root-n inference, and gives conservative smooth-approximation inference; it does not analyze a categorical target-only saturated off-target quotient.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add positive instrument-support probabilities P(Z=z)>0 to the maintained identification model, not only the conditional sampling experiment, and thread this condition through the definition of p and s.

Either add a second named strict comparator to Theorem 1 or phrase its extension over a clearly defined generic class of low-cardinality coarsening-IV analyses, with an explicit inclusion/open-boundary statement.
Promote the kink question after deriving a target-IV-specific local experiment that distinguishes its exact minimax frontier from Gafarov's general regularized affine procedure.

recommended_next_step: Revise the model to impose positive instrument support and repair Theorem 1's comparator chain before advancing the quotient kernel to Stage 0.
